subject: Emergency capacity lane + tiered overage schedule for ClearBay
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: ops@clearbay.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Emergency capacity lane + temporary uplift options

Hi Sam / ClearBay ops team,

Thanks for the heads up this morning — I reviewed the telemetry and I can see the spike you mentioned in the last 6 hours. We can provision a short-window capacity uplift to avoid throttling for your launch step.

High-level options I can push immediately:
- Option A: 48-hour emergency uplift (x3 baseline throughput). Overrun billed at 1.75x standard PAYG rate.
- Option B: 7-day staged uplift (x2 baseline first 3 days, x1.5 thereafter) with a blended overrun true-up: 1.4x effective rate for tokens above your committed tier for that week.
- Option C: Convert this week to a temporary reserved mini-commit (7 days) with a one-time setup fee; we would credit 30% of overrun if you convert to a monthly commit within 30 days.

I attached a provisional quote for Options A–C (provisional_quote_ClearBay_20270506.pdf). Before I push anything live, can you confirm: 1) which option you prefer, and 2) whether procurement can sign a PO today for any charge above $15k so we can expedite?

If you want, I can also open a short-term surge bridge under our emergency lane and cap the total daily spend to avoid surprises — this is the default we use for launch-day spikes.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Sr. Account Lead, Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0146

Attachments: provisional_quote_ClearBay_20270506.pdf
From: Sam Park <sam.park@clearbay.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clearbay.com
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Emergency capacity lane + temporary uplift options

Irene, thanks — appreciate the quick read.

Short answers: we need something that covers the next 72 hours. Option B looks closest to what our infra team needs, but two asks:
1) Can we get a capped blended rate at 1.25x instead of 1.4x? The launch is marketing-led and budget is tight — if you can tighten that number we can approve the spend.
2) Procurement needs the PO wording and an invoice path. They can sign by EOD if the rate is acceptable.

I looped procurement on this thread. Also, can you confirm whether switching to a monthly commit later would carry forward any credits from this uplift? That matters for our finance forecast.

—Sam
Sam Park
Head of Platform, ClearBay
sam.park@clearbay.com
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Sam Park <sam.park@clearbay.com>, procurement@clearbay.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Emergency capacity lane + temporary uplift options

Sam — appreciate the clarity. Looping in Laura and Markus to confirm approvals and the limits we can offer. Quick responses to your asks:

- Blended rate: I can offer 1.3x as a concession for this short 72-hour bridge, subject to legal/finance sign-off. 1.25x is below the band we can do without exec approval.
- PO wording & invoice path: attaching a short PO instruction doc (ClearBay_PO_instructions.docx) with the invoice email and remittance details. If procurement confirms the PO number and expected billing contact we’ll attach it to the uplift.
- Commit conversion credits: if ClearBay converts to a monthly committed tier within 30 days, we can apply a credit equal to 25% of the documented overrun charges from this uplift toward the first month’s invoice (will need deal_id and finance sign-off).

Request to Laura / Markus: can we greenlight a 1.3x blended overrun rate for a 72-hour Option B bridge (cap daily spend at $20k) and allow the 25% apply-forward credit if they commit within 30 days? If yes, I’ll finalize the quote and ask ClearBay to sign the PO.

Thanks,
Irene

Attachments: ClearBay_PO_instructions.docx
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Emergency capacity lane + temporary uplift options

Thanks for the context. I approve a one-off concession to 1.3x for a 72-hour staged uplift with the following guardrails:
- Daily spend hard cap at $20k (no auto-burn beyond that).
- Apply-forward credit of 25% to first month only if ClearBay signs a monthly commit >= their baseline within 30 days.
- Legal to review the PO wording for any commitments language; finance to create DEAL-9421 record and track the uplift as a short-term amendment.

Markus — please confirm this won’t break our revenue recognition. If finance is happy, we can finalize and I’ll send a short approval to Sam.

Laura Bennett
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Emergency capacity lane + temporary uplift options

Laura / Irene — finance checked: acceptable with the guardrails. We will log DEAL-9421 as a short-term uplift amendment and treat the uplift revenue as deferred over the uplift period; apply-forward credit will be issued as a contra if ClearBay migrates to a monthly commit per Laura's condition. No revenue recognition breakage on our side.

Irene — go ahead and finalize the quote at 1.3x, attach the PO instructions, and ask procurement to provide PO# and billing contact. Once we have the signed PO, ops can activate the 72-hour staged uplift and we’ll monitor.

Markus Klein
VP, Finance (Revenue Ops)
markus_klein@redwood.com
